newsitem.title: USA: L.A. County to sell $1.3 bln notes unenhanced.
newsitem.headline: L.A. County to sell $1.3 bln notes unenhanced.

text.p: Los Angeles County's short-term notes received the highest ratings possible, allowing it to issue $1.3 billion of debt next week without enhancement, county finance officials said Friday.

In a victory for the county, which has endured painful budget cuts in recent years, Moody's Investors Service Inc rated the county's short-term notes MIG-1, Standard & Poor's Corp rated them SP-1-plus, and Fitch Investors Service Inc assigned it an F-1-plus grade.
The ratings are the highest offered for short-term notes.
"Over the past five years it's been a rough road," S&P director Chris Irwin said. "It looks like the corner has been turned. The fiscal condition is stabilizing."
Moody's said the county's proposed budget was "significantly less vulnerable than recent years' budgets." Moody's also cited the county's improved liquidity position.

The strong short-term ratings will allow the county to issue $1.3 billion of tax and revenue anticipation notes on June 18 without a letter of credit, Maureen Sicotte, the county's director of public finance, said.
For the last two years, the county has been forced to buy letters of credit because of concerns on Wall Street about the its fiscal condition.
The ratings awarded to the county this week were a sign that "L.A. County is back," Sicotte said.
The county estimated that the new ratings would save taxpayers at least $2 million this June because a letter of credit for the $1.3 billion of notes will not be needed.
